chapter_theme: The all-pervader (சர்வ வியாபி): the Lord is the inner light in the body, the elements, the sun, the breath and the gods, spread through every direction, world and sea, near and far, many and yet one, and no one can trace his course. The chapter, and the book's last tantra, closes with a verse on Mulan's three thousand Tamil verses.
structure_note: The Lord as the light within the body and its lights (3026 to 3031); the Lord as all things, gods, directions, worlds and elements, often in refrains on அவனே and நின்றனன் (3032 to 3045); a closing verse on Mulan's work (3046). The grouping is mine. 3035 repeats 2857 and 3044 is close to 1722.

3026.reading: This is the Siva-enjoyment that fits; apart from it, the one light and the knowing awareness, through the limiting adjunct of maya, take on what is great and what is made, and his pervasion is his own.
3026.nuance: சிவபோகம் (the enjoyment of Siva), மாயா உபாதி and வியாபகம் are technical, and lines 3 and 4 (ஏய பரிய புரியும் தனதுஎய்தும் சாயும்) are too compressed to construe with confidence. The verse seems to say that the pervasion is the Lord's own, while its appearance as many comes through maya's adjunct; that is a reading, not the verse's plain words.

3027.reading: There is no room to seek that reality by my own knowing, and knowing it there one swells on the way; when the bright flame that breathes within, knowing the flesh, itself knows, one can reach him there too.
3027.nuance: The first line denies that 'I' can find him by searching; the last puts the knowing in the inner flame (ஒண்சுடர்), usually taken as the soul lit by grace, or as the Lord within. விம்மிடும் (swells, overflows) may be the swelling of joy or of weeping.

3028.reading: In this noisy world ringed by the sea, living in the body and seeking the light within, one can see the god who dwells inside the body as plainly as the crowding waves of the sea.
3028.nuance: கடல் frames the verse: the sea round the world in line 1 and the sea's crowding waves in line 4. Whether the waves are an image of plainness, of the Lord's countless forms, or of the restless mind through which he is seen is not fixed by the verse. கௌவை may be 'noise' or 'scandal'.

3029.reading: The lord of the gods, who is the inner light in the three great lights and stands knowingly as the body, leaves the great flame and goes along with every place of strife, as sedge spreads far and wide.
3029.nuance: The three great lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. பல்கோரை (many sedges) and இகலிடம் (places of strife) are obscure; the sedge that spreads and goes with the water may picture a pervasion that reaches even the world's conflicts.

3030.reading: Those who fell in the end, caught in the inner karma that came in with their resolve, are a wound; the divine form is the inner light in the small one, and for those who gain it the higher beings become the great flame.
3030.nuance: Each line turns on a -தியின் form (உறுதியின், இறுதியின், சிறுதியின், பெறுதியின்) made for the rhyme, and their senses are guesses. இரணம் may be 'wound' or 'debt'. The plain contrast is between those who fall by karma and those who gain the inner light.

3031.reading: The supreme flame, supreme within what one holds, the threefold light that ripens in all things and sprouts, gives a steady place as thought within the forehead; that is the great ascetic who stood as the other one.
3031.nuance: நெற்றியின் உள்ளே நினைவாய் is taken by tradition as meditation fixed between the brows. மூன்றொளி is again the three lights, and மாதவன் may be 'the great ascetic' (Siva) or Mal (Vishnu); மற்றவனாய் நின்ற (who stood as the other) allows either.

3032.reading: He is the god in each of the ten directions, the one who commands the seven worlds of wide waters, the one who comes to be, seated in every world, and as the one with the tongue he speaks.
3032.nuance: Each line ends on a -வன் noun (தேவன், ஏவன், ஆவன், நாவன்), so the verse makes its claim by naming him in four roles; நாவனும் ஆகி நவிற்றுகின்றான் makes the Lord the speaker in all speech, and perhaps in this book.

3033.reading: The watching Garuda and the lord of the earth who guards the seven worlds in an instant are in him; my spotless one, the unborn, removes karma, and does not join in going and coming.
3033.nuance: Garuda is traditionally the one whose glance draws out snake poison, and the lord who guards the worlds is taken as Vishnu, whom Garuda bears. Read so, the verse sets the gods' protection beside the Lord's removal of karma; போக்கும் வரவும் (going and coming) is birth and death.

3034.reading: The one of rich matted hair, whose body is like red gold, though withdrawn joins with everything together; the Lord is gone from nowhere and born nowhere, and stands equally with the seven shining worlds.
3034.nuance: ஒழிந்தனனாயும் (though withdrawn, or though he has ceased) against ஒருங்குடன் கூடும் gives the paradox of the one apart who is with all. ஒழிந்திலகு in line 4 is unclear: perhaps ஒளிர்ந்திலகு (shining).

3035.reading: He is awareness and he is life, he is union and he is the senses; though bound up with all he cannot be reached by thought, and he stays close as scent in a cluster of flowers.
3035.nuance: A repeat of 2857 with two different words: புணர்வும் (union) for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (lovers' sulking). Here the pair is no longer love's union and quarrel but union and the senses, which fits this chapter's pervasion of all the faculties. The scent in the flower is the one image for being in all and unseen.

3036.reading: Our father, the holy one without the scent of sense-knowledge, is in goodness the practice of the way of knowledge, and spreads everywhere in the many forms the Vedic seers speak of, keeping within.
3036.nuance: Each line opens with a -மையின் or -மையில் form (புலமை, நலமை, விலமை, பலமை); விலமை is not an ordinary word and line 3 cannot be construed with confidence. புலமையின் நாற்றமில் may mean 'untouched by the senses' or 'not smelling of learning'.

3037.reading: As the heavenly one he is above the seven worlds, as the earthly one he is for the seven seas that circle; as the cool one he stands in his own nature, and becoming the eye he stands mingled.
3037.nuance: The refrain of -அவன் names (விண்ணவன், மண்ணவன், தண்ணவன், கண்ணவன்) moves from heaven to earth to his own nature to the eye that sees. தண்ணவன் (the cool one) may hint at the moon he wears, and கண்ணவன் at his being the seer within all seeing.

3038.reading: He stood as Mal and as the four-faced one, stood as the earth below and above, stood as the tall great mountains and the seven seas, and stood as rich fruit.
3038.nuance: நின்றனன் opens every line, the chapter's main refrain. He stands as the other gods of creation and preservation and not only above them; the last line's ripe fruit (வளம் கனி) may be the fruit of the world or the sweetness he is to those who reach him.

3039.reading: Our father, the great holy one, is lord of the worlds; he is the mighty driver who presses on in the world, he becomes the many rare souls, and that is how people came to be bewildered into calling him alone God.
3039.nuance: அரும்பல சீவனும் ஆகும் (he becomes the many souls) is as strong a statement of oneness as the book makes; within Siddhanta it is taken as his pervading the souls, not being them. மாலுற்றவாறே is unclear: மால் may be bewilderment, love, or Mal (Vishnu), giving 'how Mal came to call him God' or 'how love made us call him God'.

3040.reading: He stands as the unwasting breath that shines within, as the lord of spreading rays who moves in the sky, and as the wind that moves over the earth; he is the thought that moves out from the eye.
3040.nuance: The verse matches places to powers: within, the breath; in the sky, the sun; on earth, the wind; in the eye, thought or meaning (கருத்து). பிராணன் and வாயு are both the breath, the one inside and the one outside.

3041.reading: The Supreme who made number and letter, the kinds of action, the music and the skill in that way: in the thought that the eye takes in, this and that, he stands within, melts one, and becomes one's company.
3041.nuance: The first two lines make the arts of knowledge his creation. Lines 3 and 4 are obscure: அதுஇது (that, this) may be the things perceived, and ஓர் ஆயமும் ஆமே may mean he becomes a companion, a crowd, or a gain (ஆயம் as income).

3042.reading: He who wears the holy konrai on his rich matted hair dwelt mingled everywhere, with the seed, so that the eight directions, the cosmic sphere and the underworld that exist rise up with form together with him.
3042.nuance: கருக்கொடு (with the embryo or seed) suggests that he is in things as their seed, as in the bindu chapter, but the verse doesn't say so. Line 2 (உருக்கொடு தன்னடு ஓங்க) reads தன்னடு, probably for தன்னொடு.

3043.reading: No one knows the course of the Lord through the whole world that has gone along with many things; he is far and near, the unwavering Sankara, the first, our first, skilled in standing as the one that is not many.
3043.nuance: சேயன் அணியன் (far one, near one) is a common pairing in Saiva hymns. பலவிலதாய் நிற்கும் closes the verse that opened with பலவுடன்: present with many things, he stays not-many.

3044.reading: He who is that knowledge is the primal ancient one; the Lord stood so that nothing could know him; Nandi, who knows this, is our lord, and he is the eight worlds common to all.
3044.nuance: Close to 1722: lines 2 and 3 share most words, but 1722 ends with the Lord taking the poet's body as his temple and this verse ends with Nandi, the guru, as the one who knows. பொதுஅது வான (become common) for 1722's புதுஉணர்வான (of new awareness) changes the epithet of the eight worlds.

3045.reading: He is water, earth, sky, fire and wind, and the light that dwells in the body; his name is the Supreme beyond the supreme, Pinakan, our Lord, and he who rides is the all-containing, the unwasting.
3045.nuance: The five elements and the light in the body echo the old list of the Lord's eight forms, though the verse names only six. தூரும் and ஊரும் சகலன் are unclear: ஊரும் may be 'who rides (the bull)' or 'whose town'; சகலன் may mean the all-containing or, in Siddhanta usage, the one in the sakala state.

3046.reading: The three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke, the three hundred mantras Mulan spoke, the thirty teachings Mulan spoke: the three that Mulan spoke are one.
3046.nuance: The verse speaks of Mulan in the third person, like 99, and may be a later colophon. It doesn't say what the three hundred mantras and thirty teachings are; they are sometimes taken as other works ascribed to Tirumular and sometimes as parts of this one. The claim is their unity, not their contents.

links.note: Nearly the same verse. 2857 makes the Lord union and lovers' sulking (புணரும், புலவி); 3035 makes him union and the senses (புணர்வும், புலனும்), so the love pair becomes a list of faculties he pervades. Both end on the scent in the flower cluster.

Nearly the same verse: the Lord stood where nothing could know him, and the eight worlds. 1722 ends with his taking the poet's body as his temple; 3044 ends with Nandi as the one who knows this, our lord.
Both turn on the same line, the bright flame that knows the flesh and breathes within. 1797 asks who could know the Lord if that flame did not; 3027 answers that when it knows, one can reach him.

Both place the Lord by the same four stations, within (உண்ணின்ற), in the sky (விண்ணின்று), on earth (மண்ணின்ற) and in the eye (கண்ணின்ற). 449 names him the light within and the gem in the eye; 3040 the breath within, the sun, the wind and thought.
The Kural calls number and letter (எண், எழுத்து) the eyes of living beings; Tirumular makes the Supreme their maker and goes on to the eye that takes things in. Learning's two eyes become his gift.
Both name the Lord as ஆதி, the first: the Kural makes the world have Adi Bhagavan as its first, as letters have அ; Tirumular calls Sankara 'the first, our first', present with all the world yet one.

Both open with the same line on the three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke. 99 makes the work Nandi's grace and promises the Lord to those who recite it; 3046 adds three hundred mantras and thirty teachings and declares the three one.

source_issues: 3035 repeats 2857 with two variants that change the sense: புணர்வும் for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (lovers' sulking).

3044 is a variant of 1722: line 1 அதுஅறி வானவன் ஆதிப் புராணன் for அது வுணர்ந் தோன்ஒரு தன்மையை நாடி, line 3 பொதுஅது வான for புதுஉணர் வான, and line 4 ends with Nandi as 'our lord' instead of the Lord taking the poet's body as his temple.
3042: line 2 reads தன்னடு ஒங்க, probably for தன்னொடு ஓங்க.
3031: line 4 is divided மற்றவ னாய்னி ன்ற, a misprint for மற்றவ னாய்நின்ற.
3026, 3029 (பல்கோரை), 3030, 3036 (விலமை) and 3041 (lines 3 and 4) are obscure and may be corrupt; 3034 line 4 (ஒழிந்திலகு) may be a misreading.
